data_flow: The `README.md` section will trace the end-to-end data flow of a Phase 4 planning round: 1. Room creation and `T1` (`scope.captured`): The caller creates a room (`POST /rooms`) and posts `T1` (`POST /rooms/:roomId/events`) with `scopePaths` and `goal`; the server computes `founderGoalDigest(goal)` and stores the `founder_goal` evidence item in `room_events`. 2. Round opening (`POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round` or `PlannerLoop.runRound`): If the room is non-terminal in the journal, `PlannerRecovery.recoverRoom` runs first (`journal.verify()` + `planner.reconcile(commandId)`). Otherwise, under the room lock (L3), if the room is in `SCOPED`, `PlannerLoop` appends `T2` (`task.dispatched.planner`, transitioning `SCOPED -> PLANNING` with G2 guard facts) and, in the same database transaction (`afterTransition` taking journal lock L4), appends the `journaled` row for deterministic `cmd_planner_<32-hex>`. If the room is already in `PLANNING` after `T4` (`plan.revision_requested`) or a prior `not_sent` attempt within the 3-attempt budget (`DISPATCH_POLICY.transport_retries_max = 2`), it journals the next attempt bound to the opening `T2` or `T4` event. 3. Route authorization and pre-execution attestation: `PlannerLoop` checks `authorizeRoute` against the active `AuthorizationDocument` and calls `GatewayPlannerChannel.attest(commandId)`. On the next `POST /gateway/planner/poll`, `GatewayPlannerWorker` verifies or creates the durable command record in `<gatewayDirectory>/planner/` and calls `AgyPlannerExecutor.attest`, which checks that no lingering process exists for `BUILDROOM_PLANNER_USER` and verifies the SHA-256 of `BUILDROOM_PLANNER_AGY`, returning seat `architect`, surface `antigravity`, provider `google`, and model `gemini-4-argon`. The control plane verifies exact identity match and journals `identity_bound`. 4. Dispatch and stream-json init gate: `PlannerLoop` calls `GatewayPlannerChannel.dispatch(work)` with captured `repository`, `baseSha`, `scopePaths`, `goal`, and optional latest `T4` `revisionFeedback`. On `execute`, `AgyPlannerExecutor` creates a read-only checkout at `baseSha`, spawns `sudo -n -u <plannerUser> -- <agyPath>` with `--mode plan --sandbox --model gemini-4-argon-high --effort high`, and waits for the stream-json `init` event before writing durable running evidence (`<gatewayDirectory>/planner-evidence/`) and writing the prompt to stdin. If anything fails before stdin is written, it returns `not_sent`; once `init` is verified (`init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high'` and non-empty `conversation_id`), the Gateway reports `accepted` with `{ initModel, conversationId }` and the control plane journals `dispatched` (`BRJ:c:2`). 5. Plan completion, judgment, and atomic `T3`: When `agy` exits, `AgyPlannerExecutor` kills any remaining planner-user processes (`pkill -KILL`), removes the checkout, writes closing evidence, and returns the raw assistant text. `GatewayPlannerWorker` records `finished` and reports the parsed output on a subsequent poll/report cycle. `PlannerLoop` runs `judgeRoundPlan` (checking `PLANDOC_SCHEMA_V1`, canonical `scope_paths` within captured room scope, exact `repository` and `base_sha`, `BRJ:b:1` `planHash`, `PLAN_READY_FOR_FOUNDER_APPROVAL`, and credential redaction) and then executes `submitRoundPlan`, which commits `T3` (`plan.submitted`, `PLANNING -> PLAN_REVIEW`), `PlanStore.recordPlan` (`build_room_plans` with `xmin` check), and the journal `completed` row in a single Postgres transaction. 6. Founder inspection and decision: The Founder reads the plan via `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan` (or the `plan-<planHash>.json` file written by the harness) and submits `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision` with `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN`, atomically recording `T5` (`plan.approved` -> `APPROVED`), `T4` (`plan.revision_requested` -> `PLANNING` for the next round), or `T22` (`founder.cancel` -> `CANCELLED`) together with the bound `BRJ:d:1` `DecisionRecordRow`.
trust_and_security_boundaries: The `README.md` section will document the security and privilege boundaries enforced across the Phase 4 stack: (1) Three separated bearer-credential lanes on the control plane: `CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` for room creation, `T1` scope capture, and `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan`; `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN` exclusively for `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision` (`T4`, `T5`, `T22`) with `authorizationRef: 'founder-credential/PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN'`; and `PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN_TOKEN` exclusively for `/control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round` and `/control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal` (rejected if identical to either of the other two tokens). (2) Governed-event route isolation: `POST /rooms/:roomId/events` rejects the five planner-loop events with `403 governed_path_required` and rejects client-supplied `founder_goal` evidence items so callers cannot forge guard facts or goal digests. (3) Database role and transaction fencing: `br_app_runtime` is append-only on `command_journal_append` (migrations `0007` through `0009`) and `build_room_plans` (migration `0010_plan_store`, which enforces `xmin = pg_current_xact_id()::xid` against a `T3` row in `room_events` so no plan can be inserted outside a live `T3` transaction). Lock ordering is strictly L3 (`room_state` row lock) before L4 (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(8201015)`). (4) Outbound-only Gateway pull channel (`DEC-20260815-15` clause 2): the control plane never opens inbound connections to the Gateway; all `/gateway/planner/poll` and `/gateway/planner/report` messages are Ed25519-signed envelopes bound to the active primary Gateway session (`1880c12d-d98d-4a91-b25a-23320aa7f58a`). (5) Local OS privilege separation (`AgyPlannerExecutor`): the Gateway daemon runs `agy` in an isolated OS user account (`BUILDROOM_PLANNER_USER`) via two narrow `sudo -n` rules (spawning the SHA-256-verified root-owned `BUILDROOM_PLANNER_AGY` binary in `--mode plan --sandbox`, and running `/usr/bin/pkill -KILL -u <plannerUser>`), inside a disposable read-only git checkout (`chmod -R a-w`), rejecting any run if tool calls (`run_command`, `write_file`, `edit_file`) occur or if post-run processes or files survive. (6) Credential and prose redaction: `containsCredentialMaterial` blocks credential-shaped strings in `T1` goals, `T4` feedback, plan documents, and journal payload fields, and `planner.plan_refused` logs only sanitized refusal codes without echoing raw model prose or undeclared JSON keys.

error_and_failure_behavior: The new `README.md` section will document the fail-closed error and failure semantics built into the Phase 4 planner loop: (1) Pre-send failures (`authorizeRoute` denial, `attest` failure, `identity_mismatch`, or `planner.dispatch` returning `{ kind: 'not_sent' }` before the prompt is written to `agy` stdin) journal `failed` with `not_sent` (or the corresponding pre-dispatch classification); only `not_sent` is eligible for automatic transport retry within the 3-attempt round budget (`MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS = 3`). (2) Ambiguous transport or mid-flight errors (`dispatch` or `awaitPlan` throwing, missing `receipt.init` on the `antigravity` lane, or Gateway silence on `lost`/unknown state) journal `unresolved`, halting further automatic dispatch in that room until `PlannerRecovery.recoverRoom` reconciles the command. (3) Post-dispatch failures (`route_mismatch`, `{ kind: 'failed' }` from the planner, or `judgeRoundPlan` refusal for schema violation, non-canonical or out-of-scope `scope_paths`, `repository`/`base_sha` mismatch, non-ready `terminal_status`, or credential material) journal `failed` (`route_mismatch`, `planner_reported_failure`, `plan_invalid`, or `plan_outside_captured_scope`), leaving the room in `PLANNING` without emitting `T3`. (4) Recovery defects: under `PlannerRecovery`, if a `dispatched` command reconciles as `never_received` or with an identity/route/init mismatch, it transitions to `unresolved` (`mismatch`); an `unresolved` command only transitions to `resolved` when `reconcile` returns `reconciled` (§3.5), whereas `ambiguous` and `mismatch` remain `unresolved` and block new dispatch. (5) Executor halt (`planner-halted.json`): if `AgyPlannerExecutor` encounters a post-kill survivor process, checkout removal error, or evidence-write error, it writes a durable halt record and refuses all subsequent attestations and executions until operator remediation.
observability: The `README.md` section will describe the observability surfaces of the Phase 4 planner loop as built: (1) Structured control-plane logs (`planner.plan_refused` with sanitized `PlanRefusalReason` and no raw model prose, plus recovery and lifecycle logs); (2) Full-chain journal inspection and export via `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal` (`JournalStore.verify()`, `reconstruct()`, and `commandHistory()`) and `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round` (exposing room status, `latestT2`, `latestT3`, `latestT4`, `terminalEvent`, `commands`, and `unresolvedCount`); (3) Durable Gateway-side artifacts under `<gatewayDirectory>/planner/` (SHA-256-named command state records), `<gatewayDirectory>/planner-evidence/` (per-command execution evidence including `agySha256`, `conversationId`, `initModel`, `stdoutTail`, `stderrTail`, and `postKillSurvivors`), and `<gatewayDirectory>/planner-halted.json` on fail-closed halt; and (4) Phase 4 run-harness evidence artifacts under `PHASE4_EVIDENCE_DIR` (`attempts.json`, `plan-<planHash>.json`, `<label>-<roomId>.record.json`, and `<label>-<roomId>.record.sha256`).
